entities.name: Francisco Pizarro
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Francisco Pizarro was a Spanish conquistador who led the expedition that led to the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.

Pizarro was born in Trujillo, Spain, around 1478 and began his military career in Peru in 1511.

He captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa in 1533 and went on to found the city of Lima, which became the capital of the Spanish Viceroyalty of Peru.

Pizarro's conquest of the Inca Empire had a profound impact on the indigenous population, leading to the destruction of their culture and the displacement of their people.

The conquest also led to the exploitation of the Inca Empire's wealth and resources, contributing to the decline of the Spanish economy.

Pizarro's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the brutality and the cultural exchange that occurred during the Spanish conquest.

As he once said, 'My blood is spilled in the service of Christ, and I will not rest until I have conquered the last Inca.'
